# pi-agent-extensions
A collection of extensions for the pi coding agent, and for the dsh (DeepSeek Harness) coding agent.
## Packages
All eight Pi packages are verified against Pi 1.5.0. `pi-ask` also exercises its OSC status fallback
packages are verified against Pi 1.5.0. `pi-ask` also exercises its OSC status fallback on Pi 1.4.0.
| Package                                                                                     | Desc
ription
| `@indexyz/pi-provider-sub2api`                                     | Dynamic provider support, cac
hed model and price discovery, quota reporting, saved request modes, and Grok (xAI) entries for Sub2

API-compatible relays.      |
| `@indexyz/pi-custom-provider`
| Generic OpenAI Chat Compatible, Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses, and Ollama providers with mo

del discovery, caching, and transcript-aware Ollama tools. |
| `@indexyz/pi-continue`
| Resume an interrupted or failed turn with pi's currently sel

ected model.                                                                                     |
|
`@indexyz/pi-skill`                                                           | Codex-style `$skill
-name` invocation anywhere in a prompt.

|
| `@indexyz/pi-model-trace`
| Attribute the model actually serving pi via ModelTrace numeric fingerprinting in iso

lated sessions of the current host (`/model-trace`).                     |
| `@indexyz/pi-autocompac
t`                                               | Context compaction thresholds via `/autocompact 3
00k` or `80%`, with per-model defaults and provider and global caps.

|
| `@indexyz/pi-idle-compression`                                     | Compact a session's
context automatically after it has been idle (default 50 minutes), configurable globally, per provi

der, and per model.                   |

`input` modalities for hand-written dsh provider routes the pi-ai catalog does not describe.

|

Generate a concise session title from the first user prompt with a configurable summary model.

|
| `@indexyz/dsh-prompt-suggestions`

## Releases
Each package is versioned and released independently. A release of one package publishes only that p
ackage, and each published version is tagged `@indexyz/<name>@<version>` (for example `@indexyz/pi-s
kill@0.1.43`) with a GitHub Release carrying that version's changelog section. Every package's histo
ry is in its own `CHANGELOG.md`. The release procedure is `docs/releases.md`.
Every new npm package starts with an independent empty `0.0.0` workspace: the owner publishes it wit
h the `bootstrap` tag and configures npm Trusted Publisher before the formal version is pushed to Gi
tHub for CI publication. Follow First release of a new package for the workspace template, commands
and publisher settings.
## Layout
The repository root is a private npm workspace that holds shared tooling and documentation only. Eac
h package lives in its own root-level directory with its own `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vites
t.config.ts`, tests, and changelog: `pi-<topic>/` for a pi extension, `dsh-<topic>/` for a dsh packa
ge, which builds its own artifacts from TypeScript because the Harness loads built files rather than
sources. See `docs/architecture.md`.
## Development
Pi and dsh packages are separate plugin systems, so work on one package verifies only that package:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A pi package also runs its black-box scenarios with `node --test "scripts/e2e/pi/<name>*.e2e.ts"`, a
nd the whole Pi suite with `npm run test:e2e:pi`; try it from a checkout with `pi -e ./<name>/index.
ts`. A dsh package also needs `pnpm` and `npx playwright install chromium`. Root `npm run check` and
`npm run test:e2e` cover every package in both systems; CI runs them, and they are the gate for cha
nges to shared tooling.
Dsh build output (`lib/` and optional `client.js`) is Git-ignored; `npm pack` builds and includes it
automatically. Before installing a dsh checkout into a profile, run `npm run build --workspace @ind
exyz/<name>`, then `dsh plugin --profile web add ./<name>`.
OpenSpec is installed with the repository tooling. Run `npx openspec <command>` from the repository
root for shared changes, or from a package directory for changes to that package.
Contributors and coding agents start with `AGENTS.md`, which links the rest of `docs/`.
